reason: Recurring task: user asked to pull SEO data from GSC, GA4, and RankMySEO and update the plan doc. Episode showed repeatable traps: mismatched source windows, a RankMySEO review date differing from its homepage "last check", referral spikes distorting GA4, and noindex counts rising by design. No existing skill covers recording a dated metrics snapshot against baseline and target columns.

On 26 Oct RankMySEO issues dropped 424→229 with the review still dated 13 Oct; the drop came from 3 hand-marked rows, not a re-crawl. The agent first asserted which rows were marked, then had to correct it. The skill needs an explicit rule that unchanged review dates and hand-marked rows are not progress, and that row names must be read, not assumed.

The 26 Oct run added Ubersuggest (Neil Patel) as a fourth source for the first time. The skill covers GSC, GA4, and RankMySEO only, so the agent had to infer its crawl-date, page-count, and backlink-index handling. Its backlink count (39, DA 3) must not be merged with RankMySEO's (3 backlinks), and cross-tool scores are not comparable.

The 26 Oct section compared GSC (19 Sep–16 Oct) and GA4 (21 Sep–18 Oct) windows that were offset from the 19 Oct report and from each other, so the deltas were between-window comparisons. The skill warns about lag but not about overlap between snapshots, and the agent had to add that caveat by hand.
Trigger gap: the user asked to update "gsc, ga dan rankmyseo, serta neilpatel", and the skill's description did not name Neil Patel or Ubersuggest, so it would not route for that request.

Episode exposed four reading traps in the GSC/RankMySEO/GA4 snapshot flow: stale indexing date mislabelled as the pull date (corrected in docs/31), stale browser DOM, a silent keyword-plan cap, and GA4 key events not being markable before first fire. All belong to the skill that was loaded for this snapshot.
Folded into seo-audit-and-metrics; snapshot rules carried in references/metrics-snapshot.md.
